section: Tall units H. 210 | for base unit H. 78
source_pages: printed p.116 and p.121-125 / PDF 118 and 123-127 (p.117-120 and p.124 not extracted; the section runs printed p.116-125)
family_naming_note: SAME FAMILY AS tall_h210.json, DIFFERENT SECTION. The catalog prints these as two chapters with two letter pairs - CQ/CR for printed p.111-115 and C5/C6 here - but the physical family is one: 2100 tall on a 100 plinth, depths 350 and 620. So this file JOINS family 'Tall H.210' and declares no family-level key of its own, the same way sink_base_h58_5.json joins H.58.5. What differs between the two sections is the FRONT, and a front is a property of the unit type, not of the family.
door_versions_note: THIS FILE DELIBERATELY DECLARES NO data.door_versions, AND THE ABSENCE IS A DECISION, NOT A READING. printed p.116 does print the pair - 78 and 75 - for the lower front of every position on the page. It cannot be recorded as a FAMILY key, because door_versions merges by family and family 'Tall H.210' also holds tall_h210.json, whose own no_door_versions_note says printed p.111 prints a single elevation 210 and answers no gola question at all. Declaring it here would hand the plain full-height units a 2070 front the catalog has never printed - the identical mistake Elda Q8 was opened for at H.58.5, where a family key offers a 55,5 that one position never draws. So the split is recorded per unit type, in front_layout.gola_stack_top_to_bottom, which is exact and cannot leak. CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: 80_panel reads door_versions from the family, so the properties dialog will offer these units no 78/75 switch and will draw them in the handle version. Making door_versions section-scoped is a code change in 50_registry.rb and 80_panel.rb and is NOT made here. Evidence added to Elda Q8, 2026-08-24.
width_field_note: THE FOUR-DIGIT TAIL DOES NOT DECODE, AND THIS PAGE BREAKS IT ON ITSELF. W.45 is 0551 in the first position and 1560 in the third; W.60 is 0651 and 1660. The same two widths, the same page, two different fields - so the width field is not even section-scoped, it is POSITION-scoped. _manifest.json code_grammar.tall_units already says to read the row; printed p.116 is the cheapest proof of it yet found, because both readings sit on one sheet.
extraction_note: printed p.116 taken WHOLE: three positions, twelve codes, both depths, verified against a 175-dpi render (learned rule 10) after pdftotext agreed with it line for line. Nine pages of this section remain - printed p.117-125 - and they are what the Avenida Primavera wall actually needs: the oven housings are printed p.121-123 and the fridge unit p.125. Recorded in _manifest.json catalog_map so the picker shows them grey rather than silent. | 2026-08-25, DEMAND-DRIVEN SECOND PASS: printed p.121, 122, 123 and 125 read at 600 dpi and held - 8 types, 14 codes, all d.62. Two positions on those sheets are read and NOT held: printed p.121 position 3 (C68654 / C68754), whose single mixed elevation the front_layout shapes cannot express and which is an Elda question, and printed p.123 position 3 (C62691), which is a 1320-tall wall-hung unit printed inside an H.210 section and therefore a different family. printed p.117-120 and p.124 remain unread. Account: claude/findings-2026-08-25-tall-h210-appliance-columns.md.

front_layout.gola_grouping_note: THE PAGE THAT CORRECTS THE GOLA RULE. Read at 900 dpi 2026-08-25: there is a recess hook above the FIRST 18 and NONE between the two 18s, then a hook above the 36. Two recesses, three fronts - so the PAIR of drawers gives 30 mm between them, 1,5 cm each, and the jumbo gives its own 30. The rule is: A RECESS IS SUBTRACTED FROM THE FRONT GROUP BENEATH IT, and a group of two splits it equally. Every other position held so far is a group of one, which is why the older sentence - 'the lower front gives its 30 mm' - survived this long.
